summary: Harlon Carter shot dead a Mexican American teenager in Laredo in 1931, later led the US Border Patrol through Operation Wetback, then seized control of the NRA in 1977 and turned it into a hardline gun lobby.

evidence.note: Carter born August 1913 in Granbury, Texas
1931 shotgun killing of 15-year-old Ramon Casiano and murder conviction
joins Border Patrol in 1936 and heads it by 1950
Operation Cloudburst plan to use troops, fences and roadblocks against Mexican migrants
Operation Wetback deports over a million people and extends Border Patrol inland
NRA president 1965-67, then placed in charge of the new lobbying arm
builds direct-mail fundraising operation with Richard Viguerie
1977 convention takeover makes Carter executive vice president
NRA blocks consumer-safety oversight of defective firearms
NRA-backed 2005 law shielding gun makers from lawsuits
Carter dies of lung cancer in 1991; Knox dies 2005

notes: NRA listed as co-primary since descriptions pair it with Carter. The long opening on colonial and Jim Crow gun laws (1680 onward) is background and excluded from covered_span; end year 2010 reflects the Emerson/Heller/McDonald and PLCAA segment. main_span end 1985 (end of Carter's NRA tenure) is from general knowledge; transcript does not give it. Transcript spells Knox as Neil.
